stemMd: At the same temperature, solution P has pH 4 and solution Q has pH 6. How do their hydrogen-ion concentrations compare?

options.label: A
options.textMd: P has 10 times the concentration of Q.

options.label: B
options.textMd: P has 100 times the hydrogen-ion concentration of Q.

options.label: D
options.textMd: P has twice the concentration of Q.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Q has 100 times the concentration of P.

explanationMd: A one-unit pH difference corresponds to a factor of ten. Here the difference is two units, so the ratio is 10² = 100. Since P has the lower pH, it has the greater hydrogen-ion concentration.

distractorRationale.d: The pH scale is logarithmic, not linear.
distractorRationale.e: Lower pH means higher hydrogen-ion concentration.
distractorRationale.c: Different pH values imply different hydrogen-ion activities under this model.
distractorRationale.a: That corresponds to a difference of one pH unit, not two.
